bill-clinton.body_append:
## The Constitution Avenue bookshop encounter

On a Sunday morning some years after the Athens meeting, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) and his visiting brother spotted two limousines parked outside the small Barnes & Noble in the National Press Club at roughly 14th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue. Out walked [Bill Clinton](/wiki/bill-clinton) with his daughter Chelsea, both carrying books. Kiriakou, unsure what else to say, shouted *"keep abortion safe and legal, Bill,"* to which Clinton replied *"I'm trying,"* walked over and shook Kiriakou's hand — a second, unrelated encounter Kiriakou cites as evidence that Clinton was, in person, *"the smoothest"* of the modern presidents he met.<Cite t="38:00" /><Cite t="38:21" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says [Hillary Clinton](/wiki/hillary-clinton) was *"impossible"* to deal with when she came back as a returning senator to the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](/wiki/senate-foreign-relations-committee), on which she had briefly sat before being named Secretary of State — *"impossible at that level"*?
hillary-clinton.body_append:
## Post-Athens: the Parthenon scowl and the Senate return

Extending the Athens 1999 account already cited from other appearances, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) recounted the same scene again on the PBD Podcast: [Hillary Clinton](/wiki/hillary-clinton) stepped off the elevator with Chelsea *"with this puss on her face,"* and cut short her husband's attempt at small talk about their morning at the Parthenon with *"Jesus Christ, [Bill](/wiki/bill-clinton), it's raining all day. I'll be in the room."*<Cite t="42:28" /><Cite t="42:59" /> Kiriakou adds a further characterisation from his own time on the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](/wiki/senate-foreign-relations-committee) staff: Clinton, who had briefly sat on the committee before becoming Secretary of State, *"used to come back all the time and she was impossible"* — *"impossible at that level."*<Cite t="44:04" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said the Department of Justice rescinded the subpoenas in the [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan) investigation without explanation days after naming veteran U.S. Attorney Joe DiGenova the lead investigator — leaving him *"deeply worried"* the case will not proceed?

… that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) argues the Justice Department should pursue [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan) on a conspiracy charge because it would carry a ten-to-twenty-year exposure and, so long as the cover-up continues, *"reset the statute of limitations literally every single day"*?
john-brennan.body_append:
## The 2026 DiGenova subpoena rescission

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) told the PBD Podcast in April 2026 that he was *"deeply worried"* the Justice Department had quietly abandoned the criminal investigation of [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan). Just at the start of that week, he said, the veteran U.S. Attorney Joe DiGenova — *"a giant"* — had been named the lead investigator in the Brennan case in South Florida. Then, without explanation, the subpoenas were rescinded.<Cite t="1:06:23" /><Cite t="1:06:53" />

Kiriakou said he had been told the alleged conduct fell into the category of *"process crimes"* — lying to Congress, for example — which grand juries are typically reluctant to indict on. He argued the Department should instead pursue a conspiracy charge: the conspiracy to deny [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) the presidency, he said, was ongoing so long as the cover-up continued, which meant the statute of limitations *"resets literally every single day"* and the exposure — ten or twenty years in federal prison — was more than commensurate with the conduct.<Cite t="1:07:24" /><Cite t="1:07:56" /><Cite t="1:08:26" /> He restated his personal assessment of Brennan, a man he says he has known for thirty-five or thirty-six years: *"a malevolent figure in modern American politics and government"* who *"really did attempt to carry out a coup, not with tanks in the streets"* but *"through rumour and innuendo"* to deny Trump the 51 percent of the American electorate that chose him.<Cite t="1:05:19" /><Cite t="1:12:05" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) calls the [Barack Obama](/wiki/barack-obama) administration and the outgoing [Biden](/wiki/joe-biden) administration *"a cabal of criminals"* behind their advanced degrees and smiling faces, and adds that recent Supreme Court immunity rulings benefiting [Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) *"through the back door"* also cleared [Obama](/wiki/barack-obama) of *"just about anything that he's been accused of doing"*?
barack-obama.body_append:
## 'A cabal of criminals' and the immunity backwash

On the PBD Podcast in April 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) called the [Barack Obama](/wiki/barack-obama) administration — and, extending into the Biden years, the Democratic executive apparatus — *"a cabal of criminals coming out of that Obama administration and extending into the [Biden](/wiki/joe-biden) administration."*<Cite t="34:47" /> Asked how likely federal prosecutions of Obama-era officials were, he answered that Obama himself was now legally out of reach: *"these recent Supreme Court decisions clearing [Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) also, you know, through the back door cleared Obama of just about anything that he's been accused of doing."* [Hillary Clinton](/wiki/hillary-clinton), he added, was likewise shielded — the statute of limitations having expired on *"just about everything you could possibly accuse Hillary of doing."* Only [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan), in his view, was still exposed.<Cite t="1:11:32" /><Cite t="1:12:05" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) credits Senator Ted Kennedy with the passage of [FISA](/wiki/fisa) under President Jimmy Carter in the immediate wake of Watergate, and that Section 702 — up for reauthorisation as of April 2026 — permits *"secret warrantless"* wiretaps whose threshold, he says, *"nobody will tell us"*?
fisa.body_append:
## Origins, 702, and the Carter Page test case

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) traces [FISA](/wiki/fisa) to Senator Ted Kennedy, who he says was *"instrumental in the passage of FISA"* under President Jimmy Carter in the immediate wake of Watergate, motivated by concerns about *"foreign involvement in American political machinations."* The statute created the secret court that sits on the top floor of the Justice Department — off-limits to the public, its rotating federal district-court judges permitting the [CIA](/wiki/cia) and [FBI](/wiki/fbi) to obtain warrants that cannot be released to the American people.<Cite t="1:02:13" /><Cite t="1:02:44" /><Cite t="1:03:15" />

Kiriakou treats [Carter Page](/wiki/russiagate) as the textbook demonstration of how FISA was turned on Americans it was never intended to reach: an American citizen who came under repeatedly renewed FISA warrants despite there being *"no evidence that he had ever committed a crime,"* an abuse he attributes to *"[John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan) … denying Donald Trump the presidency."*<Cite t="1:03:46" /><Cite t="1:04:48" /><Cite t="1:05:19" />

## Section 702

Kiriakou notes that Section 702 of FISA, which was up for reauthorisation as of April 2026, permits ongoing *"secret warrantless"* electronic surveillance, and that on his account nobody in government will disclose the threshold that triggers a Section 702 collection. He distinguishes the legitimate battlefield-adjacent use — identifying individuals or small groups planning terrorist attacks overseas — from what he calls the abusive domestic use, in which *"the CIA, the FBI and NSA"* pick out an interesting-looking American citizen like a podcast host and *"check him out"* despite his constitutional protection.<Cite t="1:03:46" /><Cite t="1:10:31" /><Cite t="1:11:01" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says he called the American strike on Iran three days before it happened by reading naval movements — *"if you're going to send an entire aircraft carrier strike group, you mean business; if you're going to send two of them, you're going to war. And we sent two"* — after a friend at the Pentagon told him the White House had picked *"Monday or Tuesday"*?
iran-12-day-war.body_append:
## The three-day-early prediction

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said he publicly predicted the U.S. strike on Iran three days before it happened after a Pentagon-side friend confided that the White House had settled on *"Monday or Tuesday."* He says he corroborated the tip against a piece of tradecraft he learned very early at the [CIA](/wiki/cia): *"if you want to determine American military intentions, watch naval movements."* An aircraft carrier strike group, he said, signals seriousness; two of them signals war. *"And we sent two."*<Cite t="23:25" /><Cite t="24:26" /><Cite t="24:58" /><Cite t="25:31" />

## JCPOA-like ending and the sticking point

On how the confrontation would ultimately be resolved, Kiriakou predicted the endpoint would look very much like the [JCPOA](/wiki/iran-nuclear-assessment) — *"we won it's all over we have this agreement"* — with the real sticking point being the disposition of the uranium Iran had already enriched to 60 or 80 percent, which the United States had newly insisted be transferred to it rather than to China, the United Arab Emirates or Saudi Arabia.<Cite t="29:12" /><Cite t="30:12" />

## Geopolitical fallout

Kiriakou argued the conflict had *"pushed the Iranians deeper into the embrace of China, Russia and India"* — three of the four BRICS partners named — and accelerated the day the international community either drops the [petrodollar](/wiki/petrodollar-kissinger) or begins buying oil in yuan, which he said would have a *"long-term deleterious effect on the American economy."*<Cite t="30:43" /><Cite t="31:14" /><Cite t="31:44" /> He said the Russians and Chinese were now providing Iran with targeting information *"the same way we give the Ukrainians targeting information"* — the same practice the Russians used against the United States in Vietnam.<Cite t="32:45" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) predicts [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) could stand up on national television and *"say we won, it's all over, we're coming home"* to end the [Iran confrontation](/wiki/iran-12-day-war) — an ability Kiriakou attributes to Trump's *"innate"* capacity to *"spin things better than any previous president"*?
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.body_append:
## PBD Podcast: 'Trump could spin us out'

On the PBD Podcast on 23 April 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said the American-Iranian confrontation was *"unique because [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) is president."* Trump, he said, had *"this innate ability to spin things better than any previous president"* and could plausibly appear in a national television address to declare *"we won, it's all over, we're coming home,"* concluding the crisis on his own terms.<Cite t="28:39" /><Cite t="29:12" /> He said this was the moment to *"let the diplomats do what they're trained to do,"* naming Oman, the Houthis and Algeria as the diplomatic back-channels the United States had historically used with Iran and had, in his view, underused.<Cite t="29:12" /> He characterised the divergence between the American position and the [Israeli](/wiki/iran-12-day-war) position as the real obstacle — citing the president's announcement of a ceasefire in Lebanon followed twenty-four hours later by an Israeli bombing raid as evidence that *"we have competing interests."*<Cite t="29:42" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says [Christopher Hitchens](/wiki/christopher-hitchens), who had publicly minimised [waterboarding](/wiki/waterboarding) as *"not a big deal,"* underwent a 2008 filmed demonstration, tapped out after about seventeen seconds, and thereafter suffered panic attacks for the rest of his life whenever he could not breathe for a moment?
waterboarding.body_append:
## The 2008 Hitchens demonstration

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) has invoked the 2008 filmed self-experiment of [Christopher Hitchens](/wiki/christopher-hitchens) as the canonical rebuttal to those who describe waterboarding as *"not a big deal."* Hitchens, he says, was placed on his back with a towel across his face, insisted he would be able to breathe, and tapped out after *"seventeen seconds."* More telling, in Kiriakou's account, was the aftermath: *"for the rest of his life, every time he couldn't breathe for a second, he would have panic attacks."* Kiriakou uses the anecdote to close the argument with a single line: *"Believe me, it's torture."*<Cite t="1:22:29" /><Cite t="1:23:01" /><Cite t="1:23:34" />

dyk_append: … that after [Joe Kent](/wiki/joe-kent) went public in 2026 with the identity of the American intelligence official whose leak scooped the [Iran strike](/wiki/iran-12-day-war), [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says he asked a producer for Kent's contact information so that [Veteran Intelligence Professionals for Sanity](/wiki/veteran-intelligence-professionals-for-sanity) could give him the group's Sam Adams Award for Integrity in Intelligence?
veteran-intelligence-professionals-for-s.body_append:
## Sam Adams Award to Joe Kent (2026)

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said on the PBD Podcast in April 2026 that when [Joe Kent](/wiki/joe-kent) went public with the identity of the American intelligence figure whose leak scooped the [Iran strike](/wiki/iran-12-day-war), Kiriakou immediately reached out for Kent's contact information and, on behalf of [Veteran Intelligence Professionals for Sanity](/wiki/veteran-intelligence-professionals-for-sanity), presented Kent with the group's Sam Adams Award for Integrity in Intelligence — despite the two men never having spoken directly.<Cite t="27:03" /><Cite t="27:35" />

dyk_append: … that on the PBD Podcast, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) apologised to Patrick Bet-David for having claimed on another show that Bet-David had said *"94 percent of Iranians"* backed regime change — after live ChatGPT and Grok queries during the interview pulled up published polling in the 71–92 percent range — while still calling [Reza Pahlavi](/wiki/reza-pahlavi) *"irrelevant"* and *"a clown"*?
reza-pahlavi.body_append:
## The 2026 Persian-monarchist backlash

On the PBD Podcast in April 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said his criticism of [Reza Pahlavi](/wiki/reza-pahlavi) had turned the Iranian monarchist online community sharply against him: Pahlavi, his wife and his daughter *"were following me"* and had all unfollowed him, and *"the monarchists attacked me because I called"* Pahlavi *"irrelevant"* and *"a clown."*<Cite t="04:38" /><Cite t="05:09" /> Presented on the same episode with a clip of his own earlier claim that Bet-David had cited *"94 percent"* of Iranians backing regime change, Kiriakou apologised twice on tape — *"you've shown me wrong, and I'm sorry that I perpetuated an untruth"* — after ChatGPT and Grok, queried live in the studio, produced published poll figures between about 71 and 92 percent opposing the [IRGC](/wiki/iran-12-day-war) or the Islamic Republic.<Cite t="08:17" /><Cite t="09:17" /><Cite t="09:48" /><Cite t="13:27" /> He nevertheless reaffirmed his substantive judgment that Pahlavi *"is not a strong leader,"* is *"a clown"* and is *"irrelevant."*<Cite t="05:09" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) flagged on the PBD Podcast in April 2026 a leaked report — attributed to unnamed White House sources — that [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) wants Director of National Intelligence [Tulsi Gabbard](/wiki/tulsi-gabbard) to resign after the 2026 midterm elections?
tulsi-gabbard.body_append:
## 2026 leak about post-midterm resignation

On the PBD Podcast on 23 April 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) flagged a report circulating the day before — a *"leak,"* he said, of the kind used to *"test the market"* — that [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) *"reportedly wants"* the Director of National Intelligence, [Tulsi Gabbard](/wiki/tulsi-gabbard), to resign after the 2026 midterm elections. Kiriakou treated the report as unverified and cautioned that the pattern of trial-balloon leaks made its status uncertain.<Cite t="1:37:30" /><Cite t="1:38:01" />

dyk_append: … that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) contrasts [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump)'s public defence of [FISA](/wiki/fisa) Section 702 — *"our military patriots desperately need FISA 702"* — with what Kiriakou calls Trump's own experience of the abusive [FISA Title I](/wiki/fisa) domestic surveillance under [James Comey](/wiki/russiagate)'s [FBI](/wiki/fbi)?
donald-trump.body_append:
## Kiriakou on Trump the negotiator (2026)

On the PBD Podcast in April 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said the shift in the American electorate's implicit job description of the presidency between 2000 and 2026 explained [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump)'s rise: whereas in 2000 the top qualities voters would name for a president were diplomacy and oratory, by 2026 they were *"negotiation skills,"* and Trump — unlike [Obama](/wiki/barack-obama) or [Biden](/wiki/joe-biden), *"a phenomenal negotiator"* — had matched the moment.<Cite t="33:16" /><Cite t="33:46" /> Asked whether he still supported the president if the cameras were off, Kiriakou answered *"yeah, I would say that,"* even as he acknowledged the administration had *"had problems too."*<Cite t="34:16" /><Cite t="34:47" />

## Trump on FISA 702

Kiriakou noted that Trump had drawn a personal distinction between the *"foreign"* Section 702 collection he supports — arguing it should be renewed — and the domestic *"Title I"* FISA surveillance he says was abused by *"the dirty cop [James Comey](/wiki/russiagate)"* to run the Russia collusion investigation against him. Kiriakou agreed with the distinction in principle but argued for tighter controls on Section 702 to protect the civil liberties of American citizens.<Cite t="1:09:28" /><Cite t="1:09:58" /><Cite t="1:10:31" />

dyk_append: … that on the coldest night of December 1981, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) — an eighteen-year-old George Washington University freshman — was walking around the White House when he saw the West Gate open, applauded Ronald Reagan's limousine on its way to the Kennedy Center Honors, and Reagan rolled down his window and said *"thanks for your support"*?

… that after [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou)'s felony conviction stripped his federal voting rights for life, Governor Terry McAuliffe sent an unsolicited courier to his Virginia house at seven in the morning with a hardcover envelope containing a state pardon decree bearing the gold seal — restoring his Virginia gun rights but not shielding him from the federal felon-with-a-firearm five-year mandatory minimum?

… that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says he saw a *"brilliant blinding"* orange saucer hover over Amish country on a drive with his father through the road between Newcastle and Sharon, Pennsylvania on a Friday night in 1981 — an experience later corroborated for him by an Air Force F-16 pilot cousin who said *"every pilot has seen them"*?
john-kiriakou.body_append:
## The 1981 Reagan window-down encounter

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) moved to Washington the week after he turned eighteen — one year into the presidency of Ronald Reagan, which he dates to 1982 — to attend George Washington University two or three blocks from the White House.<Cite t="35:47" /><Cite t="36:18" /> One cold December night, walking around the White House with his girlfriend, he noticed the West Gate had been left open. He waited a moment and Ronald Reagan's presidential limousine emerged, en route (as he later learned) to the Kennedy Center Honors. Kiriakou — a self-described liberal at the time who *"hated Reagan"* — nonetheless applauded because *"it's the president of the United States."* Reagan halted the limousine, rolled down the window and said *"thanks for your support."*<Cite t="36:49" /><Cite t="37:20" /><Cite t="37:51" />

## The 1999 Athens meeting and Bill Clinton

Extending accounts already given elsewhere in the corpus, Kiriakou retold on the PBD Podcast in April 2026 the story of drawing the note-taker's role for the 1999 Bill Clinton meeting with the Greek prime minister at the Intercontinental Hotel in Athens — the ambassador, Nick Burns, having *"pulled jobs out of a hat."*<Cite t="39:22" /><Cite t="39:53" /> He recounted [Bill Clinton](/wiki/bill-clinton) mistaking him for the Greek note-taker and offering him food from the untouched spread; [Hillary Clinton](/wiki/hillary-clinton) walking off the elevator scowling at the Parthenon rain; and Clinton delivering a *"vintage Clinton magic"* speech to 500 cheering Greek-American businesswomen in the hotel basement.<Cite t="40:24" /><Cite t="40:56" /><Cite t="42:59" /><Cite t="43:32" />

## The Terry McAuliffe pardon

After his 2013 felony conviction, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) lost his federal voting rights for life. He filed a routine application to Virginia's secretary of state to have his state rights restored and was told to expect an answer within two weeks. Three or four weeks later, without further contact, a courier from Governor Terry McAuliffe's office rang his doorbell at seven in the morning while he was getting his children ready for school and handed him a hardcover envelope containing a state pardon decree with the gold seal. Kiriakou had never applied for the pardon and never met McAuliffe. The state pardon restored his Virginia gun rights but did not shield him from the federal felon-with-a-firearm charge — which carries a five-year mandatory minimum — leaving the [pardon request](/wiki/kiriakou-pardon-request) directed at [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) his only route to the federal firearm rights and the CIA pension he wants back.<Cite t="1:20:23" /><Cite t="1:20:54" /><Cite t="1:21:27" /><Cite t="1:21:58" />

## The Kalshi contract

In April 2026 Kiriakou discovered his own name listed on the prediction market Kalshi as a wagerable contract on whether [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) would pardon him. On $152,000 of trading volume his implied odds sat at about 19 to 20 percent; when he tried to place a twenty-dollar bet on himself the platform blocked the trade for *"conflict of income."*<Cite t="1:16:45" /><Cite t="1:17:16" />

## The RT International licensing arrangement

Rebutting a public accusation that he was *"a communist"* and *"a spy for the Russians,"* Kiriakou said on the PBD Podcast that his weekly television show is produced by a company in Miami and *"happens to be licensed"* by RT International among other platforms — with no editorial or financial control by the Russian broadcaster. *"There are no communists running Russia anymore. Not for a very long time."*<Cite t="18:42" /><Cite t="19:14" />

## The 1981 UFO sighting

Kiriakou said on the PBD Podcast that at seventeen, on a Friday night in 1981, he and his father were driving from their home in Newcastle, Pennsylvania to a restaurant his parents had bought in Sharon, Pennsylvania — a fifteen-mile drive through unlit Amish country — when he saw a *"brilliant blinding"* flash of light, then a second and a third, and then an orange saucer that *"lit up and it's just hovering there"* about 1,200 to 1,500 feet above the road. A car pulled up behind them; the driver got out and said *"what is that?"* — before the object accelerated away *"at this fantastic speed that just defied the laws of physics."*<Cite t="1:43:42" /><Cite t="1:44:15" /><Cite t="1:44:46" /> Kiriakou said his F-16 pilot cousin — his uncle's son — later told him *"every pilot has seen them"* and that pilots filled out classified forms describing the sightings and sent them to the Pentagon. Asked on his first day at the [CIA](/wiki/cia) *"where are the UFOs,"* Kiriakou was told *"that's not what we do here. If there are any UFOs, all that stuff's at the Pentagon."*<Cite t="1:43:10" /><Cite t="1:45:50" /><Cite t="1:46:20" />

john-kerry.body_append:
## The Russell Office visit and the credenza shadow box

On the PBD Podcast in April 2026, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) retold his first visit to [John Kerry](/wiki/john-kerry)'s office in the Russell Senate Office Building, adding two details he had not emphasised elsewhere. The wall behind Kerry's desk was covered, floor-to-ceiling, with framed photographs of Kerry with world leaders *"from Gorbachev to the Dalai Lama, everybody that matters."* On the credenza by the door sat three items: a photograph of Kerry in an embrace with John Lennon, a photograph of Kerry with Peter, Paul and Mary — Kerry gave the eulogy at Mary Travers's funeral — and the shadow box containing his Silver Star, Bronze Stars and Purple Heart.<Cite t="52:20" /><Cite t="52:53" /> Kiriakou learned only afterward, from Kerry's chief of staff, that the medals Kerry had famously thrown over the White House fence to protest the Vietnam War were duplicates bought that same morning at the PX; *"those medals are the most important things in his life."* Kiriakou notes that Kerry lost his 2004 presidential race to George W. Bush by Ohio alone, an outcome *"that close,"* and that Bush's Yale grades were reportedly better than Kerry's — *"an inside joke for us"* — even though the two men were both members of Skull and Bones.<Cite t="53:24" /><Cite t="51:17" /><Cite t="51:49" />
